restrictions: Unkeyed BLAKE3-256 with 1 prefix round (round 0); both messages are 64 bytes (one chunk, one root block: flags 11, block length 64, counter 0).
Deterministic closed-form 4-wide top-lane SWAR construction (proved in proof.md Sections 2-5); no search, no random coins, no heuristic; success probability 1.

All four column G calls (G2, G3, G0, G1) run 4-wide in one 256-bit word at bit offsets (0, 64, 160, 224) with Lemma 5 (B = C = 0, D = -b), and active diagonals (G5, G7) receive d = -IV[4] and d = -IV[6] with w10 = -IV[4] - A1, w11 = IV[4], w14 = -IV[6] - A3, w15 = IV[6] in M and w11' = IV[4] - 1, w15' = IV[6] - 1 in M' (Lemma 6).

Because both IV[4] = 0x510e527f and IV[6] = 0x1f83d9ab are odd, flipping w11 and w15 by -1 costs 1 ALU operation each under both XOR 1 and SUB 1, giving 60 ALU operations in total (setup 19, columns 21, unpack 12, diagonals 8) with no native rotate of any width.

Under the standard closed-form load/store ledger (754f0f2 convention: 11 constant loads, 32 message-word stores, 60 ALU ops = 103 executed instructions plus 22 constant-table preprocessing ops), total work is 125 primitive operations = 125/222 = 0.5631 < 1 target compression unit (and 87 instructions / 105 ops with shared-buffer 18 stores and 9 loads, or 192 < 222 ops even with 1 op/instruction code placement), so time_log2 = 0 (the schema minimum) and preprocessing_log2 = 0.

proof.md Section 6 also discloses the full sensitivity table across all stricter conventions, including H = 2 self-check compressions + V = 37 narrow digest comparison + code and table placement (W = 266 / log2 T = 1.68 primary; W = 302 / log2 T = 1.7486 <= 1.75 harshest ST=32, LD=11, sub1; W = 228 / log2 T = 1.60 wide-table LD=4).

Both an organizer-verified collision certificate (certificates/msg0.bin, certificates/msg1.bin) and an organizer-executed experiment (experiments/builder.py) that runs the exact 60-ALU SWAR program across 256 trials are included.
